claim: The FileDiscovery plugin's config selector, per its own package README, is dataLayer.discovery.endpoints.pluginRef -- a three-level nesting that differs from both the llm-d.ai blog's stated dataLayer.discovery.pluginRef and the discovery.go source comment's EndpointPickerConfig.discovery.pluginRef.
stance_target: the exact EndpointPickerConfig field path used to select the file-discovery plugin -- a load-bearing API-shape detail with conflicting statements across three llm-d-authored sources
quoted_support:
Location: dataLayer.discovery.pluginRef referencing a plugin entry of type file-discovery in plugins... dataLayer:
  discovery:
    endpoints:
      pluginRef: file-discovery

claim: The FileDiscovery endpoints-file schema requires: name (string, required, unique in file), address (required, must be a valid IPv4 address -- hostnames not resolved, IPv6 not supported), port (required, string representing integer 1-65535), with optional namespace (default 'default') and labels (arbitrary key/value map).
stance_target: exact YAML/JSON schema a custom non-Kubernetes backend integration must produce to be discovered
quoted_support:
endpoints:
  - name: <string>              # required -- unique within the file
    namespace: <string>         # optional -- defaults to "default"
    address: <IPv4>             # required -- must be a valid IPv4 address
    port: <string>              # required -- integer 1-65535 as a string
    labels:                     # optional -- arbitrary key/value labels

claim: On initial load, a single invalid endpoint entry is logged and skipped (non-fatal), but file-level problems -- cannot open, cannot parse, or file size exceeding 1 MiB -- abort EPP startup entirely.
stance_target: exact failure semantics a deployer must design around when generating the endpoints file from automation
quoted_support: Each entry is validated (address must be a parseable IP, port must be in [1, 65535]) and applied via notifier.Upsert. Per-entry validation errors are logged and the entry is skipped; file-level problems (open, parse, size > 1 MiB) abort startup.

claim: With watchFile: true, the plugin explicitly handles atomic-rename and ConfigMap-style symlink-swap file updates (which destroy the inode being watched) by re-attaching the fsnotify watcher after such events, so subsequent file changes continue to be detected; endpoints present in the previous load but absent from the new one are removed via notifier.Delete.
stance_target: the FileDiscovery plugin is engineered to work correctly with common Kubernetes-style ConfigMap-mount update patterns even outside Kubernetes, e.g. atomic file replacement by an external generator script
quoted_support: After an atomic rename or ConfigMap-style symlink swap (which destroys the inode being watched), the watcher is re-attached so subsequent changes still fire... Endpoints present in the previous load but absent from the new one are deleted via notifier.Delete.

claim: Metrics for file-discovered endpoints are scraped from the same address:port that serves inference; a separate metrics endpoint per backend is not supported by the base FileDiscovery plugin.
stance_target: FileDiscovery lets an operator point metrics scraping at a different address/port than the inference traffic address for a given endpoint
scope_conditions: llm-d/llm-d-router, pkg/epp/framework/plugins/datalayer/discovery/file/README.md, main branch, fetched Sep 11, 2026 (base plugin only -- the multicluster variant relaxes this via metricsAddress/metricsPort labels)
quoted_support: Metrics are scraped from address:port (same host and port that serves inference); separate metrics endpoints are not supported.

claim: Running in file-discovery mode disables several Kubernetes-only EPP features: the InferenceModelRewrite and InferenceObjective reconcilers do not run, and any k8s-notification-source plugin configured in the data layer will not bind; the EPP emits a startup log naming these inactive features.
stance_target: non-Kubernetes (file-discovery) llm-d deployments have full feature parity with Kubernetes deployments
scope_conditions: llm-d/llm-d-router, pkg/epp/framework/plugins/datalayer/discovery/file/README.md, main branch, fetched Sep 11, 2026 -- corroborates and adds detail to the same limitation stated more loosely in the llm-d.ai blog
quoted_support: File-discovery mode runs the EPP without a Kubernetes controller manager, so several K8s-only features are inactive: the InferenceModelRewrite and InferenceObjective reconcilers do not run, and any k8s-notification-source plugin in the data layer config will not bind. The runner emits a startup log naming the inactive features.

claim: A second, previously undocumented (outside this README) discovery plugin variant, multicluster-file-discovery, exists as a cluster-scoped counterpart: it discovers peer CLUSTERS (not individual pods/processes) as endpoints, reached via a gateway host, and unlike the pod-level plugin its address field may be an RFC-1123 hostname or an IP, not IPv4-only; per-peer metrics location can be overridden via metricsAddress and optional metricsPort labels.
stance_target: existence of a second, more flexible discovery plugin (hostnames allowed, multi-cluster scoped) beyond the single-cluster/pod-level file-discovery plugin the blog described
scope_conditions: llm-d/llm-d-router, pkg/epp/framework/plugins/datalayer/discovery/file/README.md, 'Multi-cluster support' section, main branch, fetched Sep 11, 2026
quoted_support: multicluster-file-discovery is the cluster-scoped variant: it discovers peer clusters as endpoints, differing from the pod file discovery only in address validation. A cluster is reached by its gateway host, so an address may be an RFC-1123 hostname or an IP, not only an IPv4 pod address.

claim: The Ready() channel for FileDiscovery closes only after the first successful file load, letting callers gate request-serving components on the datastore being populated for the first time; this matches (and gives a concrete example of) the general Ready() contract defined in the EndpointDiscovery interface.
stance_target: concrete confirmation that FileDiscovery implements the generic EndpointDiscovery.Ready() readiness-gating contract as documented in the interface file
quoted_support: Readiness. The plugin closes its Ready() channel after the first successful load so callers can gate request-serving components on the datastore being populated.
